flows.name: PostgreSQL schema migration

steps.action: Apply ordered schema changes and ledger row in one transaction

flows.failure: Any migration error rolls back the complete transaction and leaves the previous ledger version authoritative.

invariants: Persistence sinks are technically independent; use them only where the applicable Tiingo account terms or a separate written agreement permit retention.

Starter and Trial Plan evaluation uses no persistent sink and permanently removes transient Tiingo Data immediately after the calculation or operation completes and, in all events, before the process, job, or user session ends.
When persistence is permitted, local DuckDB or Parquet can be used for package evaluation without PostgreSQL.
Where the applicable account terms permit retention, System PostgreSQL and off-host Parquet retain full history.
The rolling three-year rule applies only to Managed PostgreSQL publication.
DuckDB is not a source of record; QuansiftMarketData adds no retention period beyond the applicable provider terms.
Remote upload, manifests, retention, deletion, and publication ordering belong to the calling application and remain subject to the applicable provider terms.
Split retry durability and cross-stage retry policy belong to quansift_scheduler.
PostgreSQL schema migration uses an advisory lock and one transaction; failure rolls back both schema changes and the ledger update.
The canonical migration ledger tiingojulia_schema_migrations records the applied schema version; POSTGRES_SCHEMA_VERSION is 3.

A ledger version equal to POSTGRES_SCHEMA_VERSION is necessary but not sufficient: postgres_migration_readiness also compares the live relations against the target manifest, because a ledger row can be ahead of the columns it claims.
SyncFailure carries a category; is_quota_failure separates a provider quota rejection from a data problem, so a run that merely ran out of hourly quota is not read as a collection defect.

removed_entry_points.note: Removed, not deprecated. Calling one raises UndefVarError at the call site, which is the intended outcome: the alternative would be a silently different code path.

replacements.persistence: the PostgreSQL upsert_* overloads and write_parquet

removed_entry_points.still_supported: DuckDB connection, schema, upsert, and query primitives

package_release: Open a pull request to main and require CI to pass
Move CHANGELOG [Unreleased] into a dated section and sync Project.toml and CITATION.cff

Run the release-preflight workflow against the exact main SHA; it verifies the ref equals origin/main, runs the hermetic and PostgreSQL 17 suites, docs, links, benchmark smoke, and an image build, then records a commit status on that SHA
Tag that verified commit and push the tag
pre_registration_policy: Tag only a commit carrying a successful release-preflight status
Never create a competing tag for a version already released
production_deployment: Merge to main and tag a preflight-verified commit
Update the scheduler's [sources] rev to that tag with Pkg.add(url=..., rev=...); Pkg.update is a no-op against a pinned rev
Confirm pathof(QuansiftMarketData) reports a new package-cache hash; an unchanged hash means the fetch did not happen
Commit the scheduler's Project.toml and Manifest.toml, or the next clone reverts the pin
Pause scheduled writers and verify the system is idle before any migration
Check postgres_migration_readiness; migrate only in a deliberate window, never inside a cron run
lifecycle.deployment_note: /opt/tiingojulia is a checkout on the data-plane host that the pipeline does not load. Code reaches production through the scheduler's [sources] pin and the Pkg cache; deploying to that checkout changes nothing.
